ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory continuous screening against the OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, Spanish BOE sanctions announcements, and PEP databases under Ley 10/2010 and EU Directives 2015/849 and 2018/843. The protocol must cover all UBOs, directors, authorized signatories, and beneficial beneficiaries; enhanced due diligence is triggered upon PEP status, irregular geographic nexus, or name-based alerts. SEPBLAC filing obligations are engaged at or before incorporation as a service provider.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) — Online Denomination Certification Service (www.rmc.es)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be written in Spanish or, where statute permits, in a co-official regional language, using Latin characters compliant with Spanish orthographic rules. Non-Latin scripts or characters outside the official alphabet are rejected; foreign words must be transliterated into standard Spanish spelling. The denomination must be truthful, lawful, and not identical to an existing registered name, per Articles 2 and 4 of the Reglamento del Registro Mercantil.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the RMC issues a rejection for a proposed denomination, the applicant may first file a reconsideration request with the RMC within one month. If rejected again, a formal administrative appeal (recurso de alzada) must be submitted to the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública within one further month. Should the appeal be denied, judicial review may be pursued before the Audiencia Nacional in Madrid. The negative name certificate must be obtained and incorporated into the notarial deed within its 90-day validity window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible for the operational restaurant premises. The municipal activity and opening license (licencia de actividad/apertura) requires a physical commercial address satisfying health, fire-safety, and occupancy codes. A virtual office may serve only as a pre-incorporation correspondence address for notarial notifications, but cannot satisfy the commercial substance required for ISIC 5610 food service activity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High (estimated 80–95% probability within the first 12 months of operation). Mandatory municipal sanitary inspections, fire-safety inspections, and labor authority checks are a statutory precondition for renewing the food-service license; SEPBLAC and Registro Mercantil authorities may also inspect UBO books without prior warning.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 of 2 July 2010 (Ley de Sociedades de Capital) as amended, Articles 4, 20-23, 102-108 and 209-231; Royal Decree 1784/1996 (Reglamento del Registro Mercantil); Royal Decree 1427/1989 (Commercial Registry fee tariff); Law 30/2015 on Notarial Functions.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial (Provincial Commercial Registry of the registered office jurisdiction), coordinated by the Registro Mercantil Central, Madrid, for name reservation and national index matters.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución (notarized Public Deed of Incorporation) containing the Articles of Association (Estatutos Sociales), thereafter inscribed in the Provincial Mercantile Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: An SL must maintain minimum share capital of EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and paid up in cash at incorporation (Articles 4 and 106 LSC); the cash contribution must be deposited in a special escrow incorporation account with a Spanish-authorized credit institution, and the corresponding deposit certificate must be presented to the notary for attachment to the deed. No deferred payment is permitted for cash subscriptions.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [●] SOCIEDAD DE RESPONSABILIDAD LIMITADA, adopted unanimously by the founding members on [●] 20[●]. RESOLVED: (1) the incorporation deed executed before Notary [●] on [●] is ratified in full; (2) the subscription of 3,000 registered shares of EUR 1.00 nominal value, fully paid into escrow account no. [●] with [●] Bank, is approved; (3) the registered office is fixed at [●], Spain; (4) [●] is appointed sole Administrador with joint signature powers; and (5) the Administrador is authorized to obtain the tax identification number, pay formation expenses, file the deed at the Mercantile Registry, and execute all ancillary acts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Negative Name Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry), Madrid - electronic signature portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the official application for a negative certification of corporate name (solicitud de certificación negativa de denominación social) through the RMC online system using the advanced electronic signature of a founder or authorized agent; the registry checks the central corporate name index and, if available, issues the certificate reserving the name for a maximum three-month period; the certificate number and exact denomination must be quoted in the later public deed.
required_dossiers: RMC application form (Form CND) submitted electronically
Electronic power of representation in case of an agent applicant
At least three proposed alternative corporate names in priority order
Identification data (DNI/NIE/passport) of the founding shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the requested denomination is rejected as identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company, the system automatically examines the next alternative name; if the whole application is queried for documentation or representation defects, the applicant corrects the defect and re-files electronically; a rectified name must thereafter be the exact name incorporated in the deed of incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the Incorporation Deposit Escrow Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Credit institution authorized in Spain (Spanish bank or cooperative credit entity offering corporate formation escrow accounts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founding shareholders open a non-trading special deposit account in the name of the company in formation and transfer the full subscribed share capital (minimum EUR 3,000); the bank issues a deposit certificate (certificado de depósito) stating the amount, account number, holder and the constitution purpose; the certificate is presented to the notary at the deed execution stage.
required_dossiers: Identity documents and NIE numbers of all founding shareholders
Bank's AML/KYC forms and source-of-funds declarations
Corporate documentation of any legal-entity shareholder (bylaws, tax ID, proof of authority)
Written escrow instructions referencing the forthcoming public deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank issues a certificate not meeting notarial requirements, the credit institution re-issues the certificate on the notary's standard template; alternatively, the capital may be transferred directly to the notary's clients' escrow account, in which case the notary certifies receipt in the deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Public Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public (Notario) of the notarial district where the registered office will be situated
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founding shareholders, personally or by legal representatives, attend the notarial appointment and execute the escritura de constitución containing full bylaws and the appointment of administrators; the notary verifies identity, legal capacity, the negative name certificate and the bank escrow certificate, and, where applicable, liquidates the Documentary Legal Acts Tax (ITP/AJD) on the notarial matrix; the notary then issues the first copy (primera copia) for Commercial Registry filing.
required_dossiers: Valid negative name certificate in the exact corporate name
Bank deposit certificate evidencing full payment of the subscribed capital
Passports or national identity documents / NIE of all natural-person founders
Certificate of incorporation, bylaws, tax ID and power of attorney of every corporate founder
Draft estatutos sociales (articles of association) prepared for notarial adoption
Evidence of payment of the notarial fee estimate and any advance ITP/AJD tax deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies defects in the draft articles or in the representation documents, the founders execute an amendment deed (escritura de subsanación) before the same notary; if the bank deposit certificate is outstanding, deposit verification is obtained directly from the bank; any defect in the administrators' acceptance is cured by their confirmation statement in the deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) - Delegación de Economía y Hacienda of the province of the registered office or AEAT electronic office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form 036 (tax census declaration) with the AEAT attaching a notarially certified copy of the deed of incorporation together with the administrators' identification data; the AEAT issues the provisional NIF (a corporate number with initial letter N) used for bank account opening, invoicing and hiring before definitive registration; the filing deadline is 30 days from notarization to avoid late-filing penalties.
required_dossiers: Notarized first copy or certified copy of the deed of incorporation
Form 036 census filing signed by the tax representative or administrator
Power of attorney of the filing officer or cooperating tax agent
Identification sheet (D-01 style) and personal ID of the filing officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEAT queries the application because the deed copy lacks the registry inscription stamp (normally unavailable at this pre-registration stage), the filing is accepted with an express reservation to submit the registered copy after inscription; if the NIF issued is defective, Form 036 is amended electronically; in case of unjustified rejection, an administrative appeal (recurso de reposición) is filed through the AEAT electronic register.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the Company in the Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial of the province of the registered office (Commercial Registrar under the Ministry of Justice)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 40 days after notarization, submit the first copy of the public deed together with the negative name certificate and the completed registry entry application to the Provincial Mercantile Registry; the registrar reviews the deed against the Companies Act and the Mercantile Registry Regulation, verifies the legality of the bylaws and the appointment of officers, and upon approval issues the certificate of registration (certificación de inscripción) which constitutes conclusive proof of corporate personality.
required_dossiers: First copy of the public deed of incorporation issued by the notary
Original negative name certificate or its official registry reference
Standard registry application form (instancia de inscripción) signed by the administrator or the notary
Bank receipt of the registry fee (liquidación registral)
Supporting documentation for any clauses submitted to registry control (e.g., joint signature clauses)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the registrar issues a suspension or rejection note (calificación desfavorable), the company cures the defects by executing a supplementary rectification deed before the same notary and refiling within the priority period; the shareholders may alternatively bring a judicial appeal under Article 327 LSC; formal defects only require a short clarificatory deed, after which the entry is completed on the existing priority date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Definitive Tax Identification Number, Census Completion and Local Business Tax Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) and municipal treasury of the Ayuntamiento where the registered office is located
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registry inscription, file with the AEAT the certificate of registration together with an amended Form 036, converting the provisional NIF into the definitive NIF (the leading letter N is replaced by the final corporate letter); the company also files its definitive tax census data and, where the expected turnover exceeds EUR 1,000,000 or an economic activity is subject to the local tax, files the Impuesto sobre Actividades Económicas (IAE) declaration and any municipal administrative forms required for the activity start.
required_dossiers: Certificate of registration issued by the Provincial Mercantile Registry
Form 036 as amended for definitive NIF and administrator updates
Provisional NIF certificate and prior census acknowledgement
IAE municipal declaration (where applicable) and receipts of any local processing fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the definitive NIF is delayed because of a clerical mismatch in the registry certificate, the mismatch is corrected by obtaining a duplicate certificación registral; if the IAE assessment is incorrect, an administrative rectification request or recurso de reposición is filed with the municipal treasury while the provisional NIF remains valid for legal transactions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Opening License and Health Registration for the Food Service Establishment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ayuntamiento of the municipality of the premises (Municipal Economic Activities and Licensing Department) jointly with the Consejería de Sanidad of the pertinent Autonomous Community for sanitary registration and food business approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the technical dossier for an ISIC 5610 food-service activity, either as a comunicación previa / declaración responsable or as an application for the municipal opening license (licencia de apertura y funcionamiento), depending on the applicable municipal ordinance; attach the technical description, urban-planning compliance documentation, fire-safety certificate, acoustic report and waste-handling contracts; simultaneously notify the public health authority and apply for inscription in the Registro General Sanitario de Empresas y Alimentos (RGSEAA), presenting the food-safety self-control system (APPCC/HACCP) required by Regulation (EC) No. 852/2004; the municipal and hygiene authorities carry out on-site inspections prior to granting the final operation clearance.
required_dossiers: Municipal license application or declaración responsable form
Technical memory (memoria técnica) and layout plans of the kitchen, self-serve broth-bowl station, buffet line and dining area
Fire-safety certificate prepared by a qualified engineer under CTE DB-SI
Certificate of occupancy (licencia de primera ocupación) or equivalent building-use certificate
Waste-management contract, fat-trap service contract and environmental noise documentation required by the municipal ordinance
RGSEAA health registration application and HACCP/APPCC self-control manual
Power of attorney of the administrator or a licensed technical agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality orders corrective works or suspends the opening, the operator implements the deficiencies and requests a re-inspection; in case of denial, the company may file a recurso de alzada or reposición and, ultimately, a contentious-administrative appeal; incomplete sanitary files are cured within the statutory ten-day period in most autonomous communities to avoid archival of the RGSEAA application.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Dirección General de Actividades Económicas or equivalent municipal licensing directorate of the competent Ayuntamiento for the opening license; for food establishment registration, the Dirección General de Salud Pública of the Consejería de Sanidad of the Autonomous Community; environmental compliance reviews are handled by the environmental administration of the same Autonomous Community.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia de Apertura y Funcionamiento (Municipal Opening and Operation License) together with the inscription in the Registro General Sanitario de Empresas y Alimentos (RGSEAA) and, where applicable, the Declaración Responsable de Inicio de Actividad for the fast-casual food service operation.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Quality and Assessment Directorate of the Autonomous Community (e.g., Dirección General de Calidad Ambiental, Comunidad de Madrid), with state-level coordination by the Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico (MITERD) under Act 21/2013 on Environmental Assessment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category III (Simplified Environmental Substantiation / Memoria Ambiental). The activity is not listed under Annexes I or II of Act 21/2013, so no full Environmental Impact Assessment report is required; the municipal environmental ordinance nevertheless requires a brief environmental justification (noise, ventilation, odors, waste management) which is evaluated in the opening-license dossier.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharged to the municipal sewer must comply with the applicable Ordenanza de Vertidos: suspended solids not exceeding 500 mg/L, oils and fats not exceeding 250 mg/L, pH within 6.0-9.0; kitchen extraction systems must be fitted with certified grease filters and meet atmospheric pollutant thresholds under Decree 833/1975 for cooking-generated particulates and volatile organic compounds (VOCs); ambient and occupational noise must stay within municipal limits (typically 45 dBA daytime and 35 dBA night-time at the nearest protected receiver); used cooking oil, solid organic waste and packaging fractions must be segregated and treated by authorized waste carriers in accordance with Act 7/2022 of 8 April 2022 on waste and contaminated soils.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certificate issued by a qualified engineer or authorized inspection body certifying compliance with CTE DB-SI (fire extinguishers, marked evacuation routes, emergency lighting and occupancy-load controls); structural load verification of the self-serve broth-bowl line, buffet counters, storage racking and dining-room floor against the building certificate of occupancy; occupational health and safety clearance under Act 31/1995 on Occupational Risk Prevention, including the mandatory risk evaluation, external prevention service contract, employee hygiene and food-safety training, and documented workplace injury and emergency procedures.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Spanish SL entities obtain NIF automatically upon incorporation via Registro Mercantil; foreign-owned entities submit application to Agencia Tributaria with passport, incorporation documents, and proof of address to secure statutory TIN and VAT ID.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box; Spain applies territorial entity-level taxation with limited hybrid mismatch and CFC rules under EU directives.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory Factura Electrónica (FEL) real-time invoicing with digital stamping via AEAT API; full clearance and reporting for all taxable supplies.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT on goods exported outside the EU or qualifying offshore services to non-EU recipients; requires proof of export and non-EU destination.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or Air Waybill
Inward Remittance Certificate or proof of payment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Penalties up to 100% of VAT due plus interest and criminal sanctions; retrospective clawback for fraudulent or unsubstantiated zero-rating claims.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), operating within the euro-area framework of the European Central Bank; foreign-exchange and foreign-investment administration is also subject to the Spanish Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business and applicable EU legislation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain uses the euro, which is freely convertible for current-account and capital-account transactions. EU Treaty protections generally prohibit restrictions on capital movements, subject to sanctions, anti-money-laundering controls, tax enforcement, prudential measures, and national-security or public-policy exceptions. An SL may receive foreign equity, shareholder loans, royalties, and trade payments through regulated banks. Dividend and profit remittances are generally permitted after approval of annual accounts, satisfaction of mandatory reserve requirements, application of applicable withholding tax, and confirmation that the distribution does not impair legally required solvency or net-equity tests. Non-resident payments may be subject to Spanish withholding tax, commonly 19% for dividends and interest before treaty, EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive, or other applicable relief. Related-party royalties, management fees, and interest require arm's-length support and transfer-pricing documentation. Foreign direct investment filings or prior authorizations may apply depending on investor residence, sector, transaction value, and national-security rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain has no general statutory requirement to surrender export proceeds to the Banco de España and no mandatory conversion ratio or universal statutory conversion deadline. Export receipts may generally remain in euros or foreign currency and may be credited to Spanish or permitted foreign accounts, subject to the bank's compliance procedures, payment-services rules, sanctions screening, tax records, customs documentation, and applicable statistical or foreign-investment reporting. The company must retain invoices, contracts, transport evidence, customs declarations, bank confirmations, and accounting records supporting the commercial purpose and ultimate beneficial owner of the transaction. Banks may request timely evidence of shipment, delivery, or collection before releasing or processing funds.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for operational payments and SEPA collections, but not a complete substitute for a Spanish commercial-bank relationship. EU-authorized electronic-money institutions and payment institutions may provide IBAN accounts, card acquiring, payment execution, and foreign-exchange services under passporting rules. Safeguarded electronic-money balances are not equivalent to bank deposits and may not benefit from the Spanish Deposit Guarantee Scheme. An offshore or non-EU digital EMI may face passporting, agent, local-law, sanctions, and correspondent-bank limitations. A fintech account should not be relied upon as the sole account for Spanish incorporation capital, statutory banking certificates, cash-intensive restaurant deposits, payroll, tax payments, or high-value royalty flows. The EMI will require full corporate, UBO, source-of-funds, business-model, transaction-purpose, and expected-volume evidence.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Spanish law does not universally require directors or beneficial owners to appear physically at a bank branch. Remote onboarding, qualified electronic identification, video identification, or onboarding through an authorized representative may be available, subject to the bank's risk policy. A Spanish SL normally requires a Spanish tax identification number, corporate deed and registry evidence, powers of attorney, identification of directors and ultimate beneficial owners, and proof of registered office and business activity. Non-resident directors may generally act through notarized or appropriately legalized powers of attorney for incorporation and banking, but a bank may require an in-person interview, branch visit, live video call, Spanish tax-residency evidence, or additional correspondent-bank verification. Cash-intensive food operations and foreign-owned structures are more likely to receive enhanced due diligence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete or inconsistent ownership chain, nominee arrangements, bearer-like ownership, or inability to identify the ultimate beneficial owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current corporate registry extracts for every ownership layer; constitutional documents; shareholder register; certified ownership chart to the natural-person UBO; passports and proof of address for directors, shareholders, and UBOs; director resolutions; notarized or legalized documents where required; written explanation of control rights and any trust, nominee, or voting arrangements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign shareholder funding with unclear source of wealth, source of funds, or unexplained third-party remittances.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited or management accounts; tax returns; bank statements; sale agreements; dividend records; employment or business-income evidence; loan agreements; board approvals; capital-increase or shareholder-loan documents; remitter-to-company payment trail; sanctions screening results; and a written funds-flow memorandum reconciling the sender, legal basis, amount, currency, and intended use.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of a foreign EMI, personal account, unregulated payment intermediary, cash courier, or multiple unrelated remitters.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Regulatory authorization details of the payment provider; account ownership evidence; payment statements; commercial rationale; contractual relationship among payer, shareholder, and company; invoice or capital documentation; confirmation that funds originate from the disclosed shareholder or approved customer; and a prospective treasury policy limiting third-party payments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-intensive restaurant model, unusually high cash turnover, or mismatch between projected sales and declared activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease or title documentation; municipal opening and activity licenses; food-safety registrations; franchise or master-license agreement; menu and pricing model; POS and acquiring contracts; cash-handling policy; daily till-reconciliation procedure; bank-deposit schedule; projected monthly sales by payment method; VAT registrations; payroll forecast; and independent evidence of premises and operating readiness.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border royalty, management-fee, procurement, or franchise payments to related parties in higher-risk jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed intercompany agreement; beneficial-owner information of the recipient; transfer-pricing analysis; benchmarking; invoice and service evidence; intellectual-property or franchise rights; withholding-tax analysis; treaty-residence certificate where relevant; board approval; sanctions and adverse-media screening; and proof of actual performance and commercial benefit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk or sanctioned country exposure, politically exposed persons, adverse media, or unexplained intermediary involvement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced due-diligence questionnaire; certified identity documents; PEP declarations; sanctions-screening report; source-of-wealth narrative; transaction map; independent corporate and litigation searches; beneficial-purpose statement; compliance officer approval; and controls preventing prohibited counterparties, territories, vessels, or goods.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent business classification, missing statutory licenses, or account activity inconsistent with a self-service Chinese malatang restaurant and franchise model.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Spanish tax registration; CNAE or equivalent activity classification; municipal operating and food-handling permits; lease; supplier contracts; franchise license; business plan; expected counterparties; POS and merchant-acquiring setup; staffing plan; insurance; and a transaction-monitoring profile specifying expected inbound sales, supplier payments, payroll, taxes, rent, royalties, and shareholder funding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Failure to satisfy Spanish corporate, tax, beneficial-ownership, or accounting record requirements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: NIF certificate; deed of incorporation; Registro Mercantil filing; beneficial-ownership declaration; accounting policy; tax-registration evidence; annual accounts process; VAT and payroll compliance calendar; registered-office evidence; powers of attorney; and appointment details for the legal representative, accountant, and tax adviser.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route equity contributions through an account held in the SL's name at a regulated Spanish bank or EU payment provider, preferably from an account held by the disclosed shareholder. Use a clear payment reference such as 'share capital contribution', 'capital increase contribution', or 'shareholder loan under agreement'; Spain does not operate a universal bank purpose-code system equivalent to certain controlled-FX jurisdictions. For incorporation or a capital increase, obtain the bank certificate or electronic evidence required by the notary and corporate registry process, execute the relevant deed, and register the transaction. For shareholder loans, maintain a written agreement stating principal, currency, maturity, interest, repayment, subordination, and use of proceeds. Screen all remitters and counterparties against applicable EU and Spanish sanctions. Reconcile the bank statement to the corporate resolution, accounting entry, invoice or loan document, and ultimate source of funds. Assess whether the transaction requires a foreign-direct-investment filing, prior authorization, statistical declaration, or reporting to the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business. Do not route capital through directors' personal accounts, unrelated third parties, cash couriers, or undisclosed offshore intermediaries.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer and SEPA Direct Debit for euro-denominated supplier, rent, payroll, tax, and recurring operating payments where the beneficiary participates in SEPA. Use SWIFT cross-border payments, commonly represented by an MT103 legacy message or its ISO 20022 successor, for non-SEPA currencies or jurisdictions; include accurate ordering customer, beneficiary, intermediary-bank, invoice, and purpose information. Use commercial documentary letters of credit under UCP 600 for higher-risk suppliers, new counterparties, or material equipment imports, with documents such as commercial invoice, packing list, transport document, certificate of origin, insurance certificate, and inspection certificate as applicable. For franchise royalties and related-party payments, maintain the agreement, invoice, transfer-pricing support, tax-residency certificate, withholding-tax analysis, and evidence of service or licensed rights. For imports, reconcile payment to customs documentation, import VAT, EORI information, and shipping records. Apply sanctions, dual-use goods, anti-bribery, and trade-based money-laundering screening before payment release.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with a regulated bank or investment firm for forecast supplier payments, royalties, imports, or other documented exposures; execute under appropriate master documentation, define notional, maturity, settlement currency, and hedge purpose, and prohibit speculative over-hedging.

Non-deliverable forwards for currencies with restricted convertibility or limited deliverability, where offered by a regulated counterparty; document the reference rate, fixing date, settlement currency, exposure, counterparty credit terms, and applicable EMIR or other regulatory reporting.

Currency swaps or cross-currency swaps for recurring or longer-term currency exposures, including shareholder-loan or procurement exposures; assess collateral, valuation, early-termination, benchmark, and counterparty-credit provisions.

Purchased foreign-exchange options and collars may be used for documented commercial exposures, subject to MiFID II conduct, appropriateness or suitability requirements, product governance, valuation, and board-approved risk limits.

Hedging transactions should be documented under an ISDA Master Agreement or equivalent bank terms where appropriate, supported by a treasury policy, counterparty limits, confirmations, mark-to-market controls, collateral procedures, accounting treatment, and EMIR reporting or clearing analysis. Derivatives should be entered into for identifiable commercial risk and not as unapproved proprietary speculation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Report and Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after the end of the financial year (e.g., 30 April for calendar year companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to 300,000 EUR, potential administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By the 20th of the month following the end of the financial year (e.g., 20 January for calendar year companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties of 100 EUR per day, plus surcharges on unpaid tax

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after the end of the financial year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to 300,000 EUR and risk of company dissolution

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if net turnover exceeds 8,000,000 EUR or total assets exceed 4,000,000 EUR

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual update and confirmation of UBO information filed with the Commercial Registry within the annual report deadline

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 300 - 1,500 USD annually for registered office or virtual office service
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 2,000 - 12,000 USD for statutory audit, varying by company size

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate for newly created SLs on the first EUR 300,000 of taxable income and 20% on the excess for the first two tax periods, provided the company is engaged in an economic activity (not an asset-holding entity). This applies to the Chinese Malatang self-serve franchise vehicle only if new and actively operating. Standard 25% general rate otherwise. No specific franchise industry tax credit; ordinary R&D and job-creation incentives may reduce effective rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) filed electronically via the Sede Electrónica de la AEAT (Spanish Tax Agency online portal). Quarterly prepayment declarations use Modelo 202/222 through the same portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual definitive return; quarterly instalment prepayments (Modelo 202 for most entities, Modelo 222 for entities with a reduced rate or certain turnover) during October, December, and April.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 25 calendar days after the six-month period following the fiscal year-end. For a calendar-year SL (fiscal year ending 31 December), the deadline is 25 July of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) of the legal entity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SL must obtain a Spanish NIF; non-resident beneficial owners should not confuse their individual NIE/NIF with the corporate NIF.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Start date and end date of the tax reporting period (typically 01/01/XXXX to 31/12/XXXX).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The period must correspond to a full twelve-month accounting period unless special winding-up circumstances apply; for short periods filed on dissolution, date range reflects actual accounting period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Importe neto de la cifra de negocios (net turnover) from franchise operations, own-store sales, and royalty streams.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident branch owners must report Spanish-source turnover only; foreign-source self-catering income is not attributable to the Spanish SL unless permanent establishment rules apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Resultado contable del ejercicio (accounting profit or loss before tax), extracted from the annual accounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use Spanish GAAP; any difference with the foreign parent's books must be reconciled and disclosed in supplemental schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Extra-accounting adjustments (corrections for permanent and temporary differences, e.g. non-deductible fines, depreciation differences, transfer pricing adjustments).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-related party adjustments must be documented contemporaneously; failure to apply arm's length principle triggers a Box adjustment and penalty risk.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Base imponible (taxable base) after application of loss compensation and tax reliefs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Spanish-source taxable base cannot be reduced by foreign parent losses unless a tax consolidation regime has been approved; the SL is subject to Spanish entity-level taxation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cuota íntegra (gross tax liability) and, after deductions and withholding, cuota líquida.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders must respect Form 200 and Form 123 reporting for dividends distributed, and any DTA relief is processed separately, not on the Modelo 200.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing surcharge under Ley General Tributaria: 5% if filed within 3 months of the deadline, 10% within 6 months, 15% within 12 months, and 20% after 12 months, plus late-payment interest. Fixed penalties for false or incomplete data can reach EUR 150,000. Criminal sanctions apply if concealed tax exceeds EUR 120,000.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% for dividends distributed to non-resident shareholders, unless a double taxation treaty or the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (0% where the parent holds at least 5% for more than one year, with anti-abuse compliance) reduces it.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief, the non-resident recipient must obtain a valid Certificate of Tax Residence (CRF) from the country of residence, submit it to the Spanish paying entity before the payment date, and, where excess withholding was applied, file Form 210 (IRNR) with the relevant tax office within the four-year statute of limitations. The Spanish payer must maintain a copy of the CRF and, where applicable, file annual informational return Modelo 124.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic (non-treaty) rates: 19% for interest; 24% for royalties (19% for EU/EEA residents with exchange of information). Under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive, related EU parent/subsidiary companies may enjoy 0% withholding. Treaty rates typically range from 0% to 10% for royalties on franchise IP and 0% for bank interest paid to financial institutions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 10,000,000 annual net turnover (requirement to prepare and file Local File and Master File). For turnover below EUR 10 million, simplified documentation applies only if the aggregate value of related-party transactions exceeds EUR 100,000 per transaction type. Country-by-Country reporting is triggered for multinational groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not apply offshore Economic Substance Regulations; however, the general anti-abuse rule (GAAR) in Article 15 LGT, substance-over-form principles, and the `real business activity` requirement under Case Law force an SL managing a Malatang franchise to maintain premises, staff, management functions, operational control, and actual decision-making capacity in Spain. A letterbox or conduit SL receiving royalties without local substance will lose treaty protection and be subject to recharacterization, CFC rules, and penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate suppression of cash restaurant sales via unregistered or un-fiscalized POS terminals, omitting self-serve ingredient revenue, under-reporting royalty income from franchisees, and falsifying deductible overhead to reduce the taxable base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil fine under LGT Art. 191: proportional penalty between 50% and 150% of the evaded tax, plus late-payment interest. Criminal sanction under Criminal Code Art. 305 if the amount evaded exceeds EUR 120,000 per calendar year: imprisonment of 1 to 6 years plus fine of up to six times the evaded sum.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Criminal conviction may lead to imprisonment, travel bans, and disqualification from managing commercial entities. Civil liability includes joint and several payment of the tax debt, restitution of wrongfully gained amounts, and judicial orders to freeze business assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating or maintaining an SL that is subject to Spanish management but has no physical commercial premises, employees, inventory records, or operational substance, while royalties are channeled to a foreign related party or to a trust/foundation to divert taxable profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax payments are recalculated to reflect the real substance situation: Spanish-source royalty and trading income are fully taxed in Spain, deductions are denied, interest is charged, and fines under the GAAR rules can amount to 50%-150% of the recalculated tax. The Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) are not directly applicable, but the Spanish anti-abuse doctrine and CFC rules have equivalent effect.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil under civil and tax jurisprudence holds directors jointly liable for tax debts and sanctions. Directors can face court-ordered travel bans, asset-tracing procedures, disqualification, and, in aggravated cases, criminal restitution orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / UBO Non-Compliance and Cash Payment Limits
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to identify the ultimate beneficial owners (UBO) of franchisees, accepting business cash payments above EUR 1,000 from traders or above EUR 10,000 from individual operators without strictly regulated financial channels, and not filing suspicious transaction reports with SEPBLAC.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Law 10/2010 (Money Laundering Prevention) sanctions serious infringements with fines of EUR 10,000 to EUR 150,000 and very serious infringements with fines of EUR 150,000 to EUR 10,000,000, per infringement, according to the classification and level of negligence. Criminal money laundering (Art. 301 Criminal Code) carries imprisonment of up to 6 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly tolerate cash laundering or deficient KYC/UBO procedures are personally liable for civil penalties and may be prosecuted. Criminal conviction may result in imprisonment, travel bans, confiscation of franchise assets, and debarment from commercial licences.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing and Documentation Failures
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging the Spanish SL excessive royalties, brand renovation fees, central management fees, or interest to related foreign groups without contemporaneous comparability analysis; failing to prepare the Market File/Local File, or submitting inconsistent economic substance data.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Tax Agency will adjust the taxable income upward to the arm's length result, disallow the excess payment, impose late-payment interest, and apply the special transfer pricing penalty of 15% of the adjusted tax base (Art. 18 LIS and Art. 193 LGT). If documentation is absent and the adjustment is material, fraud penalties up to 150% apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and legal representatives who design or approve a transfer pricing fraud or knowingly sign inaccurate TP documentation are jointly liable for the extra tax, interest, and penalties. In criminal tax fraud cases involving TP, travel bans, freezing of personal assets, and imprisonment of up to 6 years can occur.
